newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bank Baer still sees EMU starting on time.
newsitem.headline: Bank Baer still sees EMU starting on time.

text.p: Bank Julius Baer said it expected European economic and monetary union to begin on schedule in 1999 because postponement would solve none of the problems facing the single currency and could wreck the project.

"On the basis of these considerations, our baseline scenario continues to assume that monetary union will start on time," it said in an investment research report. "At first it will consist of core Europe plus Ireland and Finland, but a year later it will already include an almost complete set of participants."
This means capital market yields will keep converging while forex rates of EMU candidates stay close to their ERM parities.
Increased competitive pressure in the EMU area should lead to low inflation and a favourable climate for interest rates.

"If the EMU project were to be abandoned (were there to be a postponement, the market's reaction would be on the same lines albeit somewhat less extreme), there would probably be a downgrading of the peripheral markets for a time, both in terms of interest rates and exchange rates (especially in those countries which were more politically unstable, e.g. Italy) while in Germany monetary policy would have to be eased again because of the currency's strength," it said.

Currency strength and perhaps the less pressing need for corporate restructuring would hit stock markets in core countries, but any correction would be cushioned to some extent by lower interest rates, Baer said.

It said the outlook for interest rates in core countries is likely to remain favourable for the time being and the dollar outlook remains fairly positive, supported by market expectations of a weak euro.
It said investment risks posed by EMU would likely manifest themselves primarily on peripheral markets, which Baer had downgraded earlier this year.

"Although the postponement debate will presumably flare up again periodically, there is no pressing need at present to make any major changes to our investment strategy," it said, adding concentrating on core markets should reduce volatility.
